title: queue-producers: answer its provider notices
prior_work: Answer this module's provider notices, judged affected by a read-only triage: capture-requests:182 (index.mjs:710 calls capture-requests leads() and acts on each row's attribution.ok, which now reads the request's principal filled from the run's principal_ai). For each, decide from your own requirements what this module must do, adapt or confirm, and add a test of your own for the change, failing with it reverted where code changes; where your requirements decide nothing, name the gap in not-verified. Edit no other module, and commit no generated file (rows.mjs, words-unreviewed.json, any dist; restore dist/*.bundle.json from HEAD if a build rewrites them). status.reason: R58 and R59 cannot be met from this module's paths: the facts they need are answered by no provider on layer/11 (1b180bff, with PR 806 f5828a4d, PR 812 81bd55e4 and notice-producers dbb6ca4edf merged; the suite passes 185/185 against them, so the re-test is done and nothing here regressed). (1) R59's level: instance-setup's placeArrivals (setup.mjs:2619) answers {name, profile, layer, profile_name, covers, found_at, note}, with no level and no place for the layer. queue-producers has no jurisdictions edge, so it cannot read the level itself. Also the held layers (jurisdictions/profiles/layers: federal, California, Alameda County, Oakland) are one branch, and no two share a place name, so a provider-made fixture cannot raise R59's 'two arrivals of layers named alike'. (2) R58's layer-rule-changed: no module's requirements or code offers a read of 'the rule keys an update changed in a layer the active chain gives' (searched build/requirements and bio-plane/src; instance-updates R1-R7, instance-setup R107-R115 and jurisdictions-b/-c state none). Building it here would mean inventing the provider's shape and hand-building its answer, which K4990 forbids. (3) What can be done now changes nothing a test can see: the producer already raises arrivals at any level, and placeArrivals answers layer equal to profile on every row (R113), so keying by layer gives the same ids. A test of it would pass with the change reverted (JOB-12). Recommendation: (a) a found mark for instance-setup: placeArrivals answers each arrival's layer level and place (from #heldLayers, R108's fields); (b) place R58's read in a provider, likely instance-updates or instance-setup, registered with queue-producers as placeArrivals is (R38's pattern), e.g. layerRuleChanges() -> [{update, version, layer, level, place, rules: [key]}], so the item can fill DEC-499's {version}, {layer} and {rules}; (c) if R59's two-alike case is to be tested at real shapes, a held test layer pair with one place name (jurisdictions); then restart this job to key by layer, read place.level.* and the DEC-499 keys (summary.level, detail.level, layer-rule-changed.*), and strike R58 and R59. Nothing was changed or committed in this attempt.
